docs.title: MSF Laravel Config
docs.text: msflib/config is the configuration-focused package in the MSF Laravel ecosystem. It provides reusable defaults, configuration primitives, and GraphQL-backed configuration resources that can be stitched into a Laravel application without forcing app-specific behavior into a shared package.

docs.title: Package purpose
docs.text:
This package is designed to provide:

  • Laravel service-provider registration
  • shared configuration models and schema fragments
  • reusable metadata for app-level settings
  • GraphQL access patterns for configuration data

docs.title: Key integration points
docs.text:
The package bootstraps Laravel and GraphQL integration through its service provider. It listens to Lighthouse schema build events and stitches the package schema into the application schema at runtime.

Event::listen(BuildSchemaString::class, function ($schemaString) use ($graphql) {
    return (new SchemaStitcher($graphql))->getSchemaString();
});

This allows the package to contribute schema types without requiring the application to manually import or maintain them.

docs.title: Composer installation
docs.text:
composer require msflib/config

The package depends on msflib/graphql, which means downstream apps using it should be configured for Lighthouse-based GraphQL support.

docs.title: Typical usage patterns
docs.text:
This package is meant for shared settings and metadata that are consumed across multiple app modules, such as:

  • system configuration entries
  • reusable domain defaults
  • shared config models exposed through GraphQL

docs.title: Local development

The package also includes formatting and static analysis commands:

docs.title: Config package
docs.text: The msflib/config package provides shared configuration and metadata patterns for the MSF Laravel ecosystem. It is intentionally generic: it focuses on package-level configuration primitives, reusable schema components, and app integration conveniences rather than business-domain specifics.

docs.title: Package responsibilities
docs.text:
This package is responsible for:

  • Laravel service-provider registration
  • shared config model support
  • GraphQL schema stitching
  • migration bootstrapping for configuration metadata

docs.title: Service provider
docs.text:
The package registers its GraphQL schema and migration loading in MsfConfigServiceProvider:

class MsfConfigServiceProvider extends ServiceProvider
{
    public function boot()
    {
        $graphql = __DIR__ . '/../graphql/schema.graphql';
        if (file_exists($graphql)) {
            Event::listen(BuildSchemaString::class, function ($schemaString) use ($graphql) {
                return (new SchemaStitcher($graphql))->getSchemaString();
            });
        }

        $this->loadMigrationsFrom(__DIR__ . '/../database/migrations');
    }
}

This ensures the package contributes shared schema fragments and migration files to the Laravel app without any manual per-app wiring.

docs.title: Integration pattern
docs.text:
The package is registered in Composer metadata through the Laravel provider list:

"extra": {
  "laravel": {
    "providers": [
      "Msflib\\Config\\MsfConfigServiceProvider",
      "Msflib\\GraphQl\\MsfGraphQlServiceProvider"
    ]
  }
}

This keeps package registration consistent with the other MSF packages.

docs.title: Typical usage
docs.text:
use Msflib\Config\Models\Setting;

$config = Setting::query()->first();

The package is intended to expose reusable config data that can be consumed by higher-level domain packages without duplicating the same assumptions across app modules.

docs.title: Operational guidance
docs.text:
• keep shared config resources generic and extendable
  • avoid app-specific behavior inside the package
  • use the schema and provider registration points for integration instead of custom app bootstrapping
  • treat this as a foundational package that downstream packages can build on top of

docs.title: GraphQL schema
docs.text: msflib/config contributes a GraphQL schema fragment for shared configuration entities and metadata. These schema types are stitched into the application schema at runtime via Lighthouse, allowing the package to remain modular while still behaving like a first-class part of the app’s GraphQL API.

docs.title: Schema entry point
docs.text: The package exposes GraphQL under graphql/schema.graphql. The exact objects depend on the package’s purpose, but the pattern is to declare reusable configuration types and supporting mutation or query operations.

docs.title: Stitching pattern
docs.text:
The service provider listens for BuildSchemaString and merges package schema content into the application schema:

Event::listen(BuildSchemaString::class, function ($schemaString) use ($graphql) {
    return (new SchemaStitcher($graphql))->getSchemaString();
});

This pattern keeps package schema concerns isolated and maintainable.

docs.title: Usage guidance
docs.text:
• keep shared configuration types broad and reusable
  • prefer generated or field-driven metadata over app-specific assumptions
  • make input validation explicit in the schema definitions
  • ensure schema names are stable across package versions
